video_title: Tailtale — Project Proposal (Generative AI and Social Media, Sasin)

slides.title: Dogs Can't Tell You What's Wrong
slides.slide_description: Full-bleed dark title card. Small 'Tailtale' wordmark, top-left. Center-right: a geometric line-art dog face illustration with animated AI scan rings and viewfinder corners. Left: three stacked stat lines — '5M+ pets in Thailand', '3.45M are dogs', '~50% call their pet "like a child"'. Course credit, bottom-left.
slides.narration: Meet a dog who can't tell you if she's anxious or just hungry. In Thailand, over three million dogs are treated like family — but they can't self-report pain, and vet access isn't always close. That's where Tailtale starts.

slides.title: Capture → Chart → Clinic
slides.slide_description: 3-step icon pipeline spanning the slide width: Capture (camera icon) → Chart (bar-chart icon) → Clinic (map-pin icon, conditional), each in a circular badge with a title, one-line description, and a tag naming the mockup screen it maps to. Dashed arrows with arrowheads connect the steps.
slides.narration: Tailtale is a browser app — no collar, no hardware. Point a webcam at your dog, or upload a clip. The app samples twenty key frames — that's the whole capture step, using a camera you already own.

slides.title: A Research-Grounded Vision-Language Agent
slides.slide_description: Full agentic-flow infographic: 20 sampled frames → vision-language model (DogFACS-prompted, emphasized node) → structured emotion payload → decision diamond ('concern threshold crossed?') branching No (saved to history) / Yes (tool call: Places API → vet map). Right side: DogFACS action-unit checklist and a live SVG confidence-arc gauge reading 92% / Hungry.
slides.narration: The model scores DogFACS cues — ears, brow, mouth — before naming a category and confidence: ninety-two percent, Hungry. A second tool only fires when truly needed.

slides.title: Why Tailtale Is Different, And Careful
slides.slide_description: Left: 4-row competitive comparison (Furbo/PetCube, PetPace, PerkyPet/PetNexa, Tailtale highlighted). Right: validation pipeline — DogFACS prompting → few-shot calibration (2 dataset chips) → held-out test set → pre-registered accuracy bar shown as a semicircular gauge with a pass/fail threshold. Footer: 'screening aid, not a diagnosis' and 'bias toward referring' badges.
slides.narration: Furbo and PetCube say your dog barked. PetPace reads vitals, not faces. Tailtale reads the face — and always says 'worth a vet check,' tested against real data first.

slides.title: What Ships Now vs. What's Next
slides.slide_description: Horizontal timeline with 3 phase cards: Phase 1 MVP (highlighted, solid) — capture, chart, clinic-finder; Phase 2 — community + avatar; Phase 3 — live video + bark reply. A dashed '12-24 month horizon' strip continues past phase 3. Footer: repo placeholder + course credit.
slides.narration: For this course, the MVP is capture, chart, and clinic-finder — that's it. The avatar, bark reply, and social feed are designed, not built. Getting the emotion read right comes first.

slides.title: Six Screens, One Flow
slides.slide_description: Six phone-frame mockups in a single horizontal row, evenly spaced edge to edge, recreated in HTML/CSS/SVG: Onboarding (DogMood AI splash), Capture (webcam viewfinder, 'Start Capture (20 frames)'), Emotion Read (Hungry! 92%, emotion-mix bars, consult-vet banner), Emotion Trend (7-day per-dog history line chart, Calm vs. Upset), Vet Referral (distress alert, map, clinic card with Call/Directions), and Community (post card with avatar, photo, caption, engagement stats, tagged 'Phase 2 concept'). Each phone sits under a caption naming the screen. Header states the recreation is code, not a screenshot or generated image.
slides.narration: Here's the flow end to end: onboarding, a twenty-frame capture, the emotion read, a trend chart per dog, a vet referral when needed — and a community feed for sharing your dog's story.
